Building Connections for 
Community-Engaged Learning 
The Leduc Center for Civic Engagement strengthened 
the university's community partnerships by hosting a 
Community-Engaged Networking Event on October 31, 2025. 
The gathering brought together faculty and representatives 
from 23 nonprofit organizations, schools, public agencies, 
and community groups to cultivate new relationships, 
deepen existing collaborations, and identify opportunities 
for community-engaged teaching, research, and service. 
Participants explored shared priorities across a range 
of pressing community issues, including environmental 
sustainability, affordable housing and homelessness, 
youth education and leadership, public health, equity 
and inclusion, workforce development, and disability and 
aging services. Conversations also generated ideas for 
future collaborations in research and program evaluation, 
marketing and communications, fundraising and 
organizational development, curriculum development, and 
event and program support. 
By creating space for meaningful dialogue and 
relationship-building, the networking event reinforced 
UMass Dartmouth's commitment to mutually beneficial 
partnerships that enhance student learning while advancing 
the well-being of the communities the university serves. The 
event laid the groundwork for future collaborations that will 
continue to connect academic expertise with community- 
identified priorities, creating lasting impact for both students 
and partner organizations.
